chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah and Muhammad ibn Yahya together raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that
the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) mobilised the people for the war against Mu'awiya for the second time. When the people assembled, he stood as a speaker and said:

All praise is for God, the One, the Unique, the Samad (the eternally besought), the Singular, Who was not from a thing and created nothing from a thing that existed. A power through which He is distinct from all things, and through which all things are distinct from Him.

So there is no attribute by which He can be attained, nor a limit in which examples can be set for Him. All elaboration of languages falls short before His attributes, and the variations of descriptions stray there, and the profundities of intellectual schools are bewildered in His dominion, and the comprehensive interpretations are cut short before the firmness in His knowledge, and veils from the unseen stand before His concealed mystery — so that even the aspiring intellects lose themselves in the lowest of its subtle matters.

So blessed is God Whom the farthest reach of ambitions cannot attain, and Whom the deep diving of astute minds cannot grasp. Exalted is the One Who has no counted time, no extended term, no bounded description. Glory be to Him Who has no beginning that has started, nor a point of termination, nor a final end that perishes. Glory be to Him — He is just as He described Himself, and the describers do not reach His description.

And He bounded all things at their creation — distinguishing them from any resemblance to Him and distinguishing Himself from any resemblance to them. He did not merge into them so that it would be said He subsists within them, nor did He withdraw from them so that it would be said He is separate from them, nor is He absent from them so that one would ask 'where?' — but, glory be to Him, His knowledge encompasses them, His making perfected them, and His preservation has enumerated them.

The hidden secrets of the atmosphere do not escape Him, nor the mysteries of the concealed darkness, nor whatever is in the highest heavens to the lowest earths. For every thing there is a preserver and a watchman, and every thing is encompassed by a thing. And the Encompasser of all that it encompasses is the One, the Unique, the Samad, Whom the vicissitudes of times do not change, and Whom the making of any thing does not burden. Rather, He said to whatever He willed: 'Be!' and it was. He originated what He created without a preceding example, without weariness, without fatigue. Every maker makes from something, but God made what He created from nothing.

Every knower learns after ignorance, but God was never ignorant and never learned. He encompassed all things in knowledge before their existence, so the coming-into-being of things brought no increase to His knowledge. His knowledge of them before He brought them into being is the same as His knowledge after their coming into being. He did not bring them into being to strengthen authority, nor out of fear of decline, nor loss, nor to seek aid against an opposing adversary, nor a competing equal, nor an arrogant partner — rather, the creatures are nurtured beings and the servants are submissive.

So glory be to Him Whom the creating of what He originated does not burden, nor the governing of what He created, nor weakness, nor pause — He is self-sufficient with what He created. He knows what He created and creates what He knows — not by pondering some newly-occurring knowledge He arrived at regarding what He created, nor does doubt enter upon Him regarding what He did not create — but an unalterable decree, a firm knowledge, and a perfected command.

He singled Himself out with Lordship and specified Himself with Oneness, and acquired glory and laudation for Himself alone, and was unique in tawhid and majesty and sublimity, and singled Himself out in praise, and was glorified through glorification. He is exalted above taking sons, and pure and sanctified beyond contact with women, and mighty and majestic beyond proximity to associates.

So there is no adversary for Him in what He created, and no equal for Him in what He possesses, and no one shares with Him in His dominion — the One, the Unique, the Samad, the Eradicator unto eternity, the Inheritor unto the furthest limit, Who was always and shall always be singular and eternal, before the beginning of the ages and after the unfolding of all affairs, Who never perishes and never is depleted.

By that do I describe my Lord. So there is no god but God — how great is His greatness! how majestic is His majesty! how mighty is His might! And He is far exalted above what the wrongdoers say, with a great exaltation.

key_terms.التَّنْزِيه: Transcendence — declaring God free from all creaturely limitations (implied throughout)
key_terms.التَّوْحِيد: Tawhid — divine unity, the central theological concept of Islam
key_terms.الرُّبُوبِيَّة: Lordship/Sovereignty — God's unique status as the Rabb (Sustainer-Lord) of all
key_terms.الصَّمَد: Al-Samad — the eternally besought, the One upon Whom all creation depends, Who depends on nothing; a uniquely Quranic divine name (112:2)
key_terms.الْمُتَفَرِّد: The Singular, the One Who stands alone without peer or partner
key_terms.الْوَحْدَانِيَّة: Oneness — divine uniqueness that admits of no comparison or partnership
key_terms.مَلَكُوت: The divine dominion/kingdom — the unseen spiritual realm of God's sovereignty

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about God's attributes in his sermon before the battle against Mu'awiya?
ai.summary: This is a magnificent theological sermon delivered by Imam Ali (peace be upon him) before the second campaign against Mu'awiya, narrated through Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). It represents one of the most profound articulations of divine transcendence (tanzih) in Islamic literature, establishing that God is utterly beyond all attributes, descriptions, categories, and even the most sophisticated rational inquiry. The sermon was delivered to warriors about to risk their lives, grounding their cause in the absolute sovereignty and incomparability of the God in whose name they acted.
